text: Early stop after two agreeing orders costs 118 calls vs 163 (-27.6%) with byte-equal picks and verdict; when orders 0 and 1 agree the third vote can only confirm the same 2-1 majority.
A deliberate tie rule beats the implicit one: disagreement answered as none_of_these raises A from 28 to 31 (W=22, L=6) at 109 calls (-33%); exact row-level delta listed in the iteration.
Single-order accuracy 28/54, 28/54, 29/54 for orders 0/1/2, all keep (order 2 strongest, p=0.001288); the three-call majority scores 28, so extra calls buy stability, not accuracy.
Accuracy ceiling: all 22 none-row misses are two-mode co-requests; perfect none-recall gives A=50/54, half-recovery gives A=39 with margin 240 vs threshold 54.
Accuracy levers are text-level and frozen: the -q instruction and the none option text are pinned by REQ-006, and the option text never names the both-and case that 22 of 22 misses are.
The four loss rows share an instruction-shaped fix: surface noun in the prompt vs requested action, e.g. OpenCode/Webflow named but quality requested.

Live cost dominated by latency: ~119 tokens/call, ~332 ms/call; a 3-call clarify ~357 tokens and ~1 s; early stop ~2.2 calls (~0.72 s). At 3 clarifies per 361 committed prompts the token cost is negligible.
A two-order shape redefines F and unstable (F assumes three orders and the gate 10*F<=3*M), so adopting it re-opens the frozen Keep Rule.
